sections.title: Describing problems
sections.content:
Vocabulary for identifying and discussing issues:
• dilemma — a situation requiring a difficult choice. She faced the dilemma of choosing career over family.
• predicament — a difficult or unpleasant situation. The company found itself in a financial predicament.
• drawback — a disadvantage. The main drawback of the plan is its cost.
• shortcoming — a fault or weakness. The report highlighted several shortcomings in the system.
• deteriorate — become progressively worse. Air quality continues to deteriorate in major cities.

sections.title: Finding solutions
sections.content:
How to talk about solving problems:
• remedy — a solution to a problem. There is no simple remedy for unemployment.
• alleviate — make less severe. The new policy aims to alleviate poverty.
• tackle — deal with a difficult problem. The government must tackle climate change urgently.
• compromise — settle by mutual concession. Both sides agreed to compromise on the terms.
• implement — put a plan into action. The company implemented new safety measures.

exercises.question: A situation where you must choose between two difficult options is a:
exercises.explanation: A dilemma is a situation requiring a choice between two equally undesirable alternatives.

exercises.question: To make a problem less severe is to:
exercises.explanation: Alleviate means to make suffering or a problem less severe.

exercises.question: A fault or weakness in a system is a:
exercises.explanation: A shortcoming is a fault or failure to meet a certain standard.

exercises.question: To actively deal with a difficult problem is to:
exercises.explanation: Tackle means to make determined efforts to deal with a problem.

exercises.question: When a situation becomes progressively worse, it:
To put a plan or decision into effect is to:
exercises.explanation: Implement means to put a decision, plan, or agreement into effect.

exercises.question: A disadvantage or negative aspect of something is a:
exercises.explanation: A drawback is a feature that reduces the value or desirability of something.

exercises.question: An agreement where both sides give up something is a:
exercises.explanation: A compromise is an agreement reached by each side making concessions.
